newsitem.title: MEXICO: GFAbaco says sells new loans to Fobaproa.
newsitem.headline: GFAbaco says sells new loans to Fobaproa.

text.p: Grupo Financiero Abaco said on Tuesday it made a new loan sale of about 4.1 billion pesos to Mexico's Bank Insurance Fund, Fobaproa, and that its bank unit, Banca Confia, had a capitalization index of 8.7 percent at the end of the third quarter.
"Recently, we completed a new loan sale to Fobaproa for an amount nearing 4.1 billion pesos," the northern banking group said in a statement reporting its third quarter results.

It said it also sold some 500 million pesos of embargoed goods to Fobaproa, 269 million pesos of which changed hands in the third quarter. Embargoed goods are goods seized by the bank due to default on debt.

Early in the year, Abaco announced plans to sell 2 billion pesos of its loan portfolio to Fobaproa, as part of a general capitalization program after it suffered deeply in the 1994-1995 Mexican banking crisis.
Between January and September, GFAbaco said it recorded a net loss of 429.4 million pesos. It gave no comparative figures.

"The net result of the bank (Confia) in the (third) quarter was a loss of 198.5 million pesos, which gives an accumulated net loss for the first nine months of the year of 423.8 million pesos," the statement said.
